messages.subject: Combining multiple datasets
parts:
Greetings and salutations,

I am looking to combine multiple .imzML for tumor vs normal analysis but have hit a bit of a snag as pixel across multiple sets have the same coordinates, this seems to prohibit combining them into a single MSImageSet. Is there a workaround for this?

Thanking you in advance

-Dmitri

messages.author: a647c82c283f7bff
messages.subject: Re: Combining multiple datasets
parts:
Here is my code:

> msset_n <- readImzML(fname1, folder)
> msset_n <- readImzML(fname2, folder)
> msset <- combine(msset_n, msset_t)
Error: SImageData contain pixels with duplicate coordinates

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Combining multiple datasets
parts:
Hi Dmitri,

Firstly, there is no "msset_t" defined in your code. I assume this is just a typo.

Can you check levels(msset_n$sample) for both datasets? My first guess would be that the sample names are the same in both datasets, but readImzML should set the sample names to be the same as the file names, so they should be different already.

Then check if there are duplicated coordinates in either dataset:

any(duplicated(coord(msset_n)))

If this is TRUE, then try dropping the pixels from duplicated coordinates:

msset_n <- msset_n[,!duplicated(coord(msset_n))]

Then try combining them.

-Kylie

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Combining multiple datasets
parts:
Usually they shouldn't have duplicate coordinates. If you didn't collect the data yourself, then I would ask whoever did.

One typical reason is if it's a 3D experiment or a multimodal experiment that has been co-registered, then the x, y, z, coordinates may be spatially transformed and be non-integer. In this case, they end up being rounded to the nearest gridded integer, which may result in duplicate coordinates.

If you do readImzML with as="MSImagingExperiment", the new classes and methods should handle this a little more elegantly, but some methods for these newer classes are still under development.

-Kylie
